sentences.text: An application under Section 389 read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 ('Cr.P.C.') has been preferred on behalf of the appellant for suspension of sentence and release on bail in FIR No. 0592/2014, under Section 354A IPC, registered at PS: Narela, Delhi.

2. Appellant has been sentenced to undergo RI for 05 years with fine of Rs. 1,00,000/- (in default of payment of fine, to undergo SI for 06 months) for offence punishable under Section 376 read with Section 511 IPC; and RI for 01 year with fine of Rs. 5,000/- (in default of payment of fine, to undergo SI for 01 month) for offence punishable under Section 506 IPC.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/05/2024 at 23:40:51 3.

Learned counsel for appellant submits that there are contradictions in statement of prosecutrix initially recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. on 29.04.2014, wherein, complainant alleged that when her son went out of the house for two minutes to run some errands, appellant had committed Harish Kumar vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64255685/
1 'Badtamiji'.

entities.text: Harish Kumar vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, in supplementary statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. recorded on the same day, prosecutrix made substantial improvements and alleged that accused, who was working at SBI at relevant time, had outraged her modesty by holding her hand, kissing her and groping her chest and in the meantime, while she tried to free herself, her son reached the spot.

4. Learned counsel for appellant further points out that PW-2 (son of prosecutrix) during his examination stated that when he rang the door bell of the house, appellant had opened the door and fled after pushing him.
However, in his statement before police PW-2 alleged that appellant had held his mother's hand, when he came back home from the market.

As such, the presence of PW-2,
having witnessed the incident is also disputed.
5. On the other hand, learned APP for State along with learned counsel for prosecutrix oppose the application for suspension of sentence.
She submits that there does not appear to be any substantive contradiction since, in the supplementary statement given by the prosecutrix, she had explained the entire incident.

6. Considering the discrepancies in the version given by PW-2 as well as improvements made by prosecutrix in the initial statement, wherein, incident was only described as 'Badtamiji', the evidence requires deeper consideration at the time of hearing of the appeal.

Considering the facts and circumstances, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
sentence of the appellant is suspended This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/05/2024 at 23:40:51 during pendency of appeal and is admitted to bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court concerned and subject to following conditions :
(i) Appellant shall provide his mobile number to the Investigating Officer (IO)/SHO concerned at the time of release; and (ii) In case of change of address, appellant shall intimate/communicate his address to the IO/SHO concerned.
Application is accordingly disposed of.
A copy of this order be forwarded to the Superintendent Jail and learned Trial Court concerned for information and compliance.

ANOOP KUMAR MENDIRATTA, J.
